answer: Operator Liability Ledger. Each new identity must be sponsored by an existing operator, who signs a binding liability note; if the identity misbehaves, penalties debit the sponsor, not the wallet. An attacker mass-creating identities needs a nebula of distinct sponsors, each exposing collateral. Sponsor history is scored, so a fresh marble of unknown operators carries little credit. Any operator can whisper a dispute with evidence, triggering automatic debit. Cost: collateral per sponsored identity, multiplied by how many sponsors an attacker must burn.
